svg.text: How the 15 m signal most likely reached Borneo
Cross-section along the great-circle path, ON3VZ to YC7ONI, around 14 UTC. Schematic: heights greatly exaggerated.
bent back just below the MUF
approx. 11,450 km in three to four hops (four drawn); bounce points are illustrative
The 15 m signal sat at about 96 % of the MUF: the F2 layer only just bends it back, at a shallow angle, so
the hops are long and few.
Equinox: the sun stands over the equator and lights both hemispheres equally, the best season for 15 m
Sunset line: on the day side the D layer absorbs a little on every pass (red rings); on the night side it
Near the equator the F layer is lifted after sunset and stays strongly ionised well into the evening.
The whole path stays far from the polar and auroral zones, so there is no auroral absorption.
EFHW sloper with its feedpoint at about 10 m, clear of the roofs: the low take-off angle (about 5 degrees)
